label: v250
changes: The family tree can now read a GEDCOM file in, not just write one out. If your family is already on Ancestry, MyHeritage, FamilySearch or Gramps, export it there and bring it straight in — no retyping.
You see exactly what it will add before anything is saved: every person, where they will be filed, and every connection it found.
Anyone already in this vault is recognised by name and left exactly as they are. The file's connections attach to the record you already have, instead of making a second copy of your own grandmother.
If two people share a name, it adds neither and says so. Guessing which Maria is which is the one mistake a family tree can't recover from.

Relatives who have died go to In Memory, with their dates written the way you'd say them — "about 1975", "between 1905 and 1907" — rather than in the file's own shorthand. Anything written about them in the file is kept as a note.
Everyone else joins Extended Birthdays. An ancestor whose birthday nobody wrote down still comes in; the tree keeps them, the birthday list simply has nothing to remind you about.
Adopted, step and foster parents survive the trip, and so do marriages and divorces.
Genealogy sites blank out living people's names before letting you export. Those are left out with a note saying why, instead of arriving as a person called "Living".
A file that would make somebody their own grandfather has that one connection refused, with the reason, and the rest still comes in.
A file that isn't a GEDCOM, is empty, or holds a whole archive rather than a family is turned down whole — never half-imported.
